newsitem.title: USA: Motorola trades up, recovery seen underway.
newsitem.headline: Motorola trades up, recovery seen underway.

text.p: Shares of technology giant Motorola Inc rose 3-5/8 to 86-1/8 on Wednesday after the company beat second quarter earnings estimates and posted growth in orders in its key businesses, analysts said.
"It's a confirmation that the earnings recovery that everyone on Wall Street has been forecasting is getting underway," said Robert Wilkes, an analyst with Brown Brothers Harriman.

Lehman Brothers analyst Todd Koffman raised his 1997 earnings per share estimate to $2.71 from $2.58, and his 1998 view to $3.65 from $3.40. In a summary report, he said Motorola was "on the road to recovery".
Late Tuesday, Motorola reported second quarter earnings of $0.62 a share excluding a $170 million one-time charge. According to First Call, the consensus estimate was $0.56 a share.
Orders in the company's two main segments, semiconductors and cellular products, were up 36 percent and 20 percent, respectively.
A cyclical downturn in the world semiconductor industry and stiff competition in cellular phones had previously plagued Motorola.
